text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on May 13 in history:
1568 - Mary Queen of Scots was defeated by the English at the battle of Langside in Glasgow.
1607 - Captain John Smith and a party of soldiers landed in Virginia at Jamestown and established the first permanent British settlement in the New World.
1619 - Johan van Oldenbarnevelt, statesman and founding father of the Netherlands, was executed by Prince Maurice of Nassau on a charge of subverting religion.
1717 - Maria Theresa, Empress of Austria and Queen of Hungary and Bohemia, was born in Vienna.
1767 - John VI of Portugal was born. Ruling first as prince regent (1799-1816) and then as king (1816-26), he formally acknowledged Brazil's independence in 1825.
1787 - The first fleet of ships carrying convicts to the new penal colony of Australia left England. They arrived the following January.
1830 - The Republic of Ecuador founded, with Juan Jose Flores as president.
1835 - John Nash, British architect famous for his developments of Regent's Park and Regent Street in London, died.
1842 - Sir Arthur Sullivan, English composer who together with librettist W.S. Gilbert produced operettas including "The Mikado", "The Pirates of Penzance" and "The Gondoliers", was born.
1846 - The U.S. Congress formally declared war on Mexico over California, although fighting had begun days earlier.
1882 - French painter Georges Braque was born. He worked closely with Pablo Picasso, jointly forming the movement known as Cubism.
1888 - Brazil's parliament decided to abolish slavery.
1907 - British novelist Daphne du Maurier (Lady Browning), granddaughter of novelist George Browning and best known for her novel "Rebecca", was born.
1913 - William R. Tolbert Jr, Liberian president from 1972 until he died in a coup in 1980, born.
1927 - "Black Friday" occurred in Germany, signalling the collapse of its economic structure.
1930 - Fridtjof Nansen, Norwegian Arctic explorer and diplomat, died. He headed Norway's team at the League of Nations and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1922
1940 - After setting up Britain's wartime coalition, Winston Churchill told parliament he could offer "....nothing but blood, toil, tears and sweat".
1941 - Martin Bormann was named head of the Nazi Party Chancellery in Germany, following Rudolf Hess's mysterious flight to Scotland.
1943 - The Italian Commander-in-Chief in Tunisia surrendered a day after his German counterpart, with the Allies holding some 250,000 prisoners of war.
1949 - The first British-produced jet bomber, the Canberra, made its first test flight.
1950 - Blind U.S. Motown legend Stevie Wonder was born as Steveland Judkins Morris.
1958 - French nationalists in Algeria rebelled against their government's policy of doing a deal with Algerian rebels, seizing government buildings and taking over several towns.
1961 - U.S. film actor Gary Cooper, who won Oscars for his roles in the films "Sergeant York" and "High Noon", died at 60.
1965 - Israel and West Germany agreed to establish diplomatic relations. Several Arab nations broke ties with Germany.
1968 - Talks between North Vietnamese and American negotiators began in Paris, aimed at ending the Vietnam War.
1981 - Pope John Paul II was shot and wounded as he drove through a crowd of 20,000 in St Peter's Square in Rome. The gunman, Mehmet Ali Agca, was arrested.

1992 - Three astronauts simultaneously walked in space for the first time. The trio retrieved and repaired the Intelsat-6 satellite from the U.S. shuttle Endeavour in a walk lasting 8 hours 29 minutes.
1993 - The Strategic Defence Initiative ("Star Wars"), the futuristic defence programme initiated by U.S. President Reagan, was downgraded by the Pentagon.
1994 - Palestinian police took over control of Jericho from Israeli soldiers.
1994 - Foreign ministers from the West and Russia agreed on a new joint strategy to relaunch Bosnian peace negotiations.
1996 - Thousands of Liberian war refugees, many ill after a week at sea, were refused admission to the Ghanaian port of Takoradi.
1996 - Over 600 were killed by a tornado in the northern Bangladesh district of Tangail.
